title: After Discard on a quit, a system quit request is still refused
why: note_unsaved_edits stores tabs.iter().any(Tab::is_dirty) and ignores CloseState::Quitting (system_quit/mod.rs:61-64). After Discard at the last question the tabs stay dirty, so the asker answers NotYet and sends Close again, although the reader has answered; on a Mac that cancels a log-out. I could not compile the proposed predicate here (a source edit was refused), so its diff is a sketch.
observable: On a Mac, a log-out or Quit that arrives between Discard and the window closing is refused; the app still closes, and the log-out has to be asked for again.
size: 2 files, about 8 lines, plus one assertion in src/app/system_quit/tests.rs
guards: src/app/system_quit/tests.rs: add assert_eq!(ask(), QuitAnswer::Now) after Discard in discard_goes_on_to_close_the_window. Coverage: the new function is one expression, hit by the existing tests. 21-F3's rename would rename CloseState here too.
repro: reproduced: `assertion left == right failed: the reader answered Discard  left: NotYet  right: Now` (system_quit/tests.rs, asker called after Discard)

options.cost: About 8 lines and one assertion; a system quit after Discard is let through.

options.cost: 2 lines in reach, but the next frame's note_unsaved_edits sets it again unless it also checks Quitting, so it ends as the first option.

options.name: Leave it
options.cost: Nothing; the window is narrow and the app still quits, but a log-out is cancelled.

title: Every frame compares the whole text of every clean tab to learn whether anything is unsaved
why: frame/mod.rs:70 calls note_unsaved_edits each frame, and Tab::is_dirty is content != saved_content, a full compare for a clean tab (lengths equal). Before this PR only the front tab paid it (edit_controls/mod.rs:53). It is against rule 5 as written, and small in practice. A cached flag is not a small change: the editor writes tab.content directly (content/mod.rs:183) and 25 lines of unit tests mutate content without calling content_edited.
diff:
sketch, not compiled
  option b
+ /// Deliberately per frame: one compare a tab. GATES.md, 'per-frame costs'.
  option a
+ dirty: bool,   // on Tab, set in content_edited, save_to_disk, apply_loaded_content
- self.content != self.saved_content
size: b: 1 comment and a GATES.md line. a: src/tab/mod.rs plus about 25 test lines that set content by hand
guards: a changes src/tab/tests.rs, close_prompt/tests.rs, system_quit/tests.rs and modal/tests.rs helpers that push to content. PR 21 adds more writers of saved_content (look_at_disk), each of which would have to refresh the flag.

options.cost: One comment and one GATES.md line; a documented exception to rule 5.

options.cost: A refactor of its own; about 25 test lines change; every writer of content or saved_content, PR 21's included, must refresh it.

options.cost: Calls at each edit, save, reload, close and answer; easy to miss one, and a missed one quits with unsaved edits.

title: The unsafe block in add_should_terminate also holds four safe operations
why: The block (mac.rs:185-201) holds the transmute and class_addMethod, and also the pointer cast, sel!, as_ptr and as_bool, all safe. Moving them out narrows what the SAFETY comment has to cover. mac.rs is compiled for macOS only, so no gate on Linux checks the edit; CI's cargo check on macos-latest does.
code:
unsafe {
        let method = std::mem::transmute::<
            extern "C-unwind" fn(
                *mut AnyObject,
                Sel,
                *mut AnyObject,
            ) -> NSApplicationTerminateReply,
            Imp,
        >(method);
        class_addMethod(
            std::ptr::from_ref(class).cast_mut(),
            sel!(applicationShouldTerminate:),
            method,
            SHOULD_TERMINATE_TYPES.as_ptr(),
        )
        .as_bool()
    }
guards: No test runs mac.rs. GATES.md's sentence 'The block holds the call ... and the transmute' stays true.

title: quit_answer is pub though only the crate and its tests call it
why: True (lib.rs:65; callers mac.rs:145 and tests.rs). But mac.rs is not compiled on Linux, so a pub(crate) quit_answer is unused there outside tests and trips dead_code under -D warnings, and the crate doc links to it (lib.rs:6), which rustdoc refuses for a private item. placement and is_off are pub for the same reason.
guards: clippy -D warnings (dead_code on Linux), rustdoc (private intra-doc link), missing_docs. crates/mac-window/src/tests.rs calls it six times and stays.

options.name: Leave it pub like placement and is_off
options.cost: Nothing; one more public function in an unpublished crate.

options.name: Make it pub(crate) behind a cfg
options.cost: 4 lines and a cfg attribute that the other two helpers do not have; the doc comment loses its link.
